facts.statement: Cruschedula is an enigmatic bird genus containing only one species, Cruschedula revola, and is considered a nomen dubium.
facts.quote: Cruschedula is an enigmatic bird genus considered to be nomen dubium which consists of the single species Cruschedula revola.

facts.statement: The genus Cruschedula was first described by Florentino Ameghino in 1899.
facts.quote: The genus was first described by Florentino Ameghino in his 1899 volume Sinopsis geológico-paleontológica. Suplemento. (Adiciones y correcciones.).

facts.statement: Ameghino named the genus Cruschedula by combining the words for "shin" and "a small sheet of paper".
facts.quote: The name was coined by Ameghino from a combination of the meaning "shin" and meaning "a small sheet of paper".

facts.statement: The genus and species were originally described based on a single partial bone that Ameghino identified as a section of a tarsometatarsus.
facts.quote: The genus and species were described from a single partial bone which Ameghino considered to be a tarsometatarsus section.

facts.statement: The fossil was found in Oligocene beds of the Deseado Formation near the San Jorge Gulf in Southern Patagonia.
facts.quote: The bone was found in Oligocene (Tinguirirican to Deseadan) beds of the Deseado Formation near San Jorge Gulf in Southern Patagonia.

facts.statement: Ameghino initially created the family Cruschedulidae but later synonymized it into Cladornithidae in 1906.
facts.quote: In his paper, Ameghino erected the family Cruschedulidae, however in his 1906 paper "Enumeracion de los Impennes Fosiles de Patagonia y de la Isla Seymour" he synonymized the family into Cladornithidae.

facts.statement: Ameghino classified the fossil as a penguin because he believed it resembled other penguin fossils found in the same formation.
facts.quote: This was because the fossil, having been collected from an outcrop of the Deseado Formation, was thought to be similar to other penguin fossils Ameghino attributed to the same formation.

facts.statement: The time range for Cruschedula is estimated from 33.9 to 23.04 million years ago.
facts.quote: Time range: Rupelian to Chattian (33.9 to 23.04 million years ago)

rejected.statement: George Gaylord Simpson argued in 1946 that the holotype lacked distinguishing features to confirm it was a penguin.
rejected.quote: After examining the holotype, Simpson concluded there were no distinguishable details that defined the bone as from a penguin, but did not have any opinion as to what bird group it may have belonged to.

rejected.statement: Pierce Brodkorb suggested in 1964 that the fossil was not a tarsometatarsus but the end of a scapula.
rejected.quote: Pierce Brodkorb, who asserted the fossil to not be a tarsometatarsus but rather the end of a scapula.

rejected.statement: Eduardo P. Tonni rejected the placement of the genus in Accipitridae, considering the original bone fragment undiagnostic.
rejected.quote: This placement was rejected by Eduardo P. Tonni in his 1980 paper The present state of knowledge of the Cenozoic birds of Argentina where he considered the bone fragment upon which the genus was erected to be undiagnostic.
